CVE-2024-0727.db6ba6191109acf9d5755063f0cdb5c4772286c0:
Reject malformed/empty CMS content with CmsException instead of NRE

CmsSignedData and CmsEnvelopedData -- and every CMS byte[]/stream parser, which
funnel through CmsUtils.ReadContentInfo -- threw NullReferenceException on empty
input and on a content-less ContentInfo (the [0] content is OPTIONAL in the
ASN.1, so a contentType-only ContentInfo is valid DER). This is the CMS sibling
of the PKCS#12 CVE-2024-0727 null-content class. Null-guard the decoded
ContentInfo at the ReadContentInfo chokepoint ("No content found.") and the
SignedData/EnvelopedData parse in the four ContentInfo ctors ("Malformed
content."), matching bc-java's CMSException guards. Found by mutational fuzzing.
CVE-2024-0727.2e2c06ac6c0bbdf35fe78a82186af0af9521cf4c:
Reject empty PKCS#12 input with IOException instead of NRE

Pkcs12Store.Load parsed the top-level PFX via Pfx.GetInstance(Asn1Object.
FromStream(input)); an empty or EOF stream decoded to null, so Pfx.GetInstance
returned null and the next access (pfx.AuthSafe) threw NullReferenceException --
an undeclared exception escaping the IOException contract (the top-level analog
of the CVE-2024-0727 null-content class; the inner content was already guarded).
Null-check the decoded PFX and throw IOException. Found by mutational fuzzing.

CVE-2023-0464.39f321ea3fab2e3f2c004345111b8efa7d28b2cc:
Bound the X.509 valid-policy-tree size during PKIX path validation

RFC 5280 policy-mapping x anyPolicy expansion (6.1.3/6.1.4) grows the
valid-policy-tree multiplicatively per certificate with no node cap, so a crafted
certificate chain could exhaust memory during path validation -- the
CVE-2023-0464 class. Add CheckPolicyTreeSize(), called once per certificate at
the end of ProcessCertD, which rejects a live node count above a configurable
maximum (default 8192, env Org.BouncyCastle.X509.MaxPolicyNodes) before the tree
grows further. Ports bc-java 01db42757d.

The test fixture is marked [NonParallelizable] because it sets the cap via an
environment variable (matching Asn1IntegerTest); without it the low cap leaks
into NistCertPathTest running in parallel.
